selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What teaching from the Qur’an is mentioned near the beginning of the passage?
questions.answer: Believers are told to perform the prayers at fixed times.

questions.question: What complaint did the older man make about the daily prayers?
questions.answer: He said praying five times every day felt too much and became tiring because it keeps continuing.

questions.question: When the speaker listened to his own self, what did he hear?
questions.answer: He heard his own self saying the same complaint.

questions.question: What was feeding this wrong way of thinking in the self?
questions.answer: Laziness and Satan were pushing it.

questions.question: What did the speaker understand about those complaining words?
questions.answer: He understood that they came from the evil side of the soul and from bad whisperings.

questions.question: Why did the speaker decide to start with his own self first?
questions.answer: Because a person who has not corrected his own self cannot properly help others.

questions.question: How does the speaker describe the condition in which the self spoke those words?
questions.answer: It spoke in ignorance, laziness, and heedlessness.

questions.question: What was the speaker planning to give his self after this?
questions.answer: He was going to give it five warnings as an answer.

questions.question: Who spoke first in the passage, and what was notable about him?
questions.answer: An elderly man with a strong body and high position spoke first.

questions.question: What good thing did the man admit before he complained?
questions.answer: He admitted that the prayers are good.

questions.question: What part of the prayers did he think was too much?
questions.answer: He thought doing them five times every day was too much.

questions.question: Did the speaker reject the man right away, or did something else happen later?
questions.answer: Later, the speaker found the same complaint inside his own self.

questions.question: What image is used to show how the self accepted this bad idea?
questions.answer: It is shown as listening with the ear of laziness.

questions.question: From whom was the self learning this complaint?
questions.answer: It was taking that lesson from Satan.

questions.question: What important character lesson did the speaker learn from this experience?
questions.answer: He learned that a person should work on fixing his own soul before trying to fix others.

questions.question: In a few words, what is the main problem being introduced in this passage?
questions.answer: The problem is feeling bored with the regular daily prayers.

questions.question: What does the verse in the passage teach about prayer times?
questions.answer: It teaches that prayer times are appointed and not left random.

questions.question: Why is that verse a good match for the story that follows?
questions.answer: Because the story is about someone complaining that the prayers happen regularly every day.

questions.question: What happened a long time after the man’s complaint?
questions.answer: The speaker examined himself and heard the same words from his own inner self.

questions.question: What made the speaker realize the complaint was not trustworthy?
questions.answer: He saw that it came through laziness and satanic whispering.

questions.question: What does the phrase about the soul commanding evil mean here?
questions.answer: It means the lower self can push a person toward wrong attitudes and actions.

questions.question: What wise step did the speaker take after understanding this?
questions.answer: He chose to begin reform by dealing with his own self first.

questions.question: Why are the coming warnings needed?
questions.answer: They are needed to answer the self’s mistaken and careless complaint.

questions.question: Name three bad states linked to the self’s complaint.
questions.answer: Ignorance, idleness, and heedlessness.
